steps.title: Label MBP‑2C protein with ATTO 488
steps.instruction: Covalently attach ATTO 488 maleimide to surface‑exposed cysteines of purified MBP‑2C.

substeps.instruction: Purify the MBP‑2C fusion protein up to the step before size‑exclusion chromatography, pool the fractions to be labeled, and determine protein concentration from 280 nm absorbance.
Dissolve ATTO 488 maleimide in water‑free DMSO to make a 10 mM stock solution; keep the sealed screw‑cap tube frozen for future use.

Add an equimolar amount of the 10 mM ATTO 488 stock to 100 µL flotation buffer, then add this mixture to the pooled protein, mix gently by pipetting, and cover the tube with aluminum foil to prevent photobleaching.
Incubate the labeling reaction at 4 °C overnight.
Quench the reaction by adding quenching mix so that the final DTT concentration is 25 mM, mix gently, and incubate at room temperature for 20 min.

Pass the labeled protein over a Superose 6 10/300 GL size‑exclusion column equilibrated with flotation buffer; record absorbance at 260, 280 and 500 nm and collect the peak (expected elution ~12.5 mL).
Calculate the degree of labeling (DOL) using DOL = (A₅₀₀ × εₚᵣₒₜ)/[(A₂₈₀ – A₅₀₀ × C₂₈₀) × εₘₐₓ].

steps.title: Prepare fluorophore‑labeled SUVs
steps.instruction: Generate small unilamellar vesicles containing POPC, POPE and DOPE‑Atto647N.

substeps.instruction: In a borosilicate glass tube, combine lipids to a total concentration of 1 mg/mL: POPC 75 mol %, POPE 24.9 mol %, DOPE‑Atto647N 0.1 mol % dissolved in chloroform. Use a microdispenser with replaceable glass capillary tips; change the tip and rinse with chloroform between uses. Handle chloroform in a fume hood with appropriate PPE.

Direct a low‑flow stream of nitrogen gas into the tube to evaporate chloroform in an ordered way without splashing (e.g., rubber tubing attached to a nitrogen outlet and a cut P1000 tip fixed with Parafilm).
Place the dried lipids in a vacuum oven overnight for complete removal of residual chloroform.
Add 500 µL flotation buffer to obtain a 2 mg/mL lipid suspension.
Cover the tube with parafilm and vortex to resuspend the lipids.
Incubate the tube in a 42 °C water bath for 15 min, then vortex again.
Transfer the suspension to a microcentrifuge tube and keep on ice.
Sonicate with a tip sonicator (10 s pulse, 20 s rest, 20 % amplitude) until the solution becomes significantly less turbid.
Centrifuge at 21,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C to pellet metal residues from the sonicator tip and any remaining larger lipid aggregates.
Remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet and discard the pellet.
Store the prepared liposomes at 4 °C; use within three days.

steps.title: Set up fluorescence flotation reaction
steps.instruction: Mix labeled protein, SUVs and TEV protease before density‑gradient ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 100 µL reaction containing 0.8 µM labeled MBP‑2C, 1 mg/mL SUVs and 8 µM TEV protease in flotation buffer.
Incubate the reaction for 2 h at room temperature; optionally verify complete MBP‑2C cleavage by SDS‑PAGE and extend incubation if needed.
Add 500 µL OptiPrep 48 to the reaction tube and mix thoroughly.
Place the mixture at the bottom of an open‑top thin‑wall ultra‑clear tube (4 mL, 11 × 60 mm).

Overlay sequentially with 800 µL OptiPrep 30, then 800 µL OptiPrep 20, and finally 2 mL flotation buffer. Use a cut P1000 tip to deposit the lower‑percentage solutions gently without disturbing the interfaces.
Ultracentrifuge the tube in an SW 60 Ti rotor at 364,000 × g for 3 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect fractions and measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Harvest gradient fractions and record protein and lipid fluorescence signals.

substeps.instruction: After centrifugation, pipette fractions from the top of the tube as illustrated, keeping the pipette tip just submerged under the surface.
Dilute each fraction to a final volume of 1 mL with flotation buffer.
Aliquot three 100 µL replicates of each diluted fraction into separate wells of a 384‑well solid black plate (triplicate readings).
Add 100 µL of OptiPrep 48, OptiPrep 30 and OptiPrep 20 as background controls.
Measure fluorescence: for protein excitation 510 nm, emission 530–540 nm; for lipid excitation 647 nm, emission 664–674 nm.

steps.title: Purify unlabeled MBP‑2C for SDS‑PAGE assay
steps.instruction: Obtain MBP‑2C protein without fluorophore labeling.

substeps.instruction: Purify the MBP‑2C fusion protein as described previously, performing the final size‑exclusion chromatography run in flotation buffer.

steps.title: Prepare unlabeled SUVs
steps.instruction: Generate small unilamellar vesicles without fluorescent lipid.

substeps.instruction: Follow the liposome‑preparation steps above, omitting DOPE‑Atto647N from the lipid mixture.

steps.title: Run flotation assay with unlabeled components
steps.instruction: Perform the same reaction, gradient setup and ultracentrifugation as in the fluorescence protocol.

substeps.instruction: Follow the steps in “Set up fluorescence flotation reaction” (excluding the fluorescence‑specific notes) and then proceed to fraction collection.

steps.title: Precipitate proteins from fractions with TCA
steps.instruction: Precipitate proteins from each gradient fraction for SDS‑PAGE analysis.

substeps.instruction: Collect fractions as described and dilute each to 1 mL with flotation buffer.
Add 120 µL of TCA solution (50 g TCA dissolved in 50 mL distilled water) to each fraction.
Vigorously shake the tubes.
Incubate the tubes on ice for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 21,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C and carefully decant the TCA supernatant.
Add 500 µL ice‑cold acetone to each tube, incubate on ice for 15 min, then centrifuge again at 21,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Decant the acetone and repeat the acetone wash once more.
Dry the tubes in a fume hood overnight to evaporate any residual acetone.
Prepare high‑pH 1× Laemmli buffer by mixing 250 µL 500 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5, 500 µL distilled water and 250 µL 4× Laemmli buffer.
Add 100 µL of the high‑pH Laemmli buffer to each tube and heat at 95 °C for 15 min.
Load the samples onto a 4%–20% gradient SDS‑PAGE gel and image the gel by a suitable method.
